final_answer: after injection, the mrna enters nearby cells (often muscle cells) without entering the nucleus. the cell machinery reads the mrna and produces the viral protein (e.g., spike protein). the protein is displayed on the cell surface, alerting immune cells like dendritic cells. these cells process the protein and present fragments to t-cells and b-cells. t-cells destroy infected cells, while b-cells produce antibodies that neutralize the virus. memory t and b cells remain, enabling faster responses upon future exposure. the mrna degrades quickly, leaving no permanent changes to dna.
